primary_source_evidence.source: GitHub Docs: Rate limits for the REST API
primary_source_evidence.observed_fact: REST requests have finite per-window primary and secondary rate limits. Authenticated-user primary limit is documented as 5,000 requests/hour; content-generating requests are generally limited to 80/minute and 500/hour. When the primary limit is exhausted, GitHub returns 403 or 429 and instructs clients not to retry until reset.

Ordinary repositories have operational and size limits, including a recommended 10 GB on-disk repository size, enforced 2 GB push size, and throttling guidance; these are repository transport constraints, not evidence that optional hosted-compute/storage quota products are required.

quota_gate.interpretation: Per-window REST throttling is not by itself a prohibited monthly/trial/paid quota under the frozen control: the control expressly models it as resumable repository transport. It must be handled across invocation boundaries with durable checkpoint/continuation rather than in-run waiting. This does not prove that GitHub repository transport is an independent durability domain or a general Phase-1 solution; it only confirms the transport carve-out and exact duplicate status for this candidate.
